name: Sophie Münstermann
title: Bystander reactions to covert and overt antisemitic discrimination
summary: Examines how observers recognize and respond to different forms of antisemitic discrimination.

name: Marie Herb
title: Jewish perspectives of social identity and social support in Germany after October 7, 2023
summary: A qualitative network analysis of semi-structured interviews about identity, relationships, and support.

name: Jana Gerber
title: Collective traumatization of Jewish people in Germany after October 7, 2023
summary: A qualitative study of how collective trauma is experienced through changes in social relationships.

name: Merit Dresing
title: Collective memory: Antisemitism and Germans’ perceptions of their role in the Holocaust
summary: Examines the relationship between contemporary antisemitism and understandings of historical responsibility.

name: Shai Vopel
title: Antisemitism and criticism of Israeli policy: A two-wave study on predictors of boycott versus engagement
summary: Distinguishes policy criticism from prejudice when examining support for different forms of political action.

name: Lucy Bergen
title: Affective polarization in adolescents: Descriptive and prescriptive inclusivity norms
summary: Examines how perceptions of what peers do and what peers approve of relate to adolescent polarization.

name: Carlos Diaz
title: Sexual and gender identities without borders: Acculturation of queer refugees in Germany
summary: Studies identity and adaptation at the intersection of migration, sexuality, and gender.

name: Laura Stritzke
title: Knowing how we feel: Perceived collective and group-based emotions in times of war
summary: Examines perceived emotional norms and group-based emotions in the context of war.
award: Gert-Sommer Prize, German Peace Psychology Forum (2024)

name: Kilian Wübbelt
title: Coping with long-COVID stigmatization: Self-compassion and illness identity
summary: Studies how self-relating and the place of illness in identity relate to experiences of long-COVID stigma.

name: Sofie Ronsiek
title: School-based social norm intervention and tolerance: Social norms and migration background
summary: Examines school-based inclusivity work, with attention to social norms and students’ migration backgrounds.

name: Antonia Krömeke
title: Flourishing in life among patients with IBD: Illness identity, coping, and quality of life
summary: Investigates how living with inflammatory bowel disease relates to identity and positive psychological functioning.

name: Inga Garbelmann
title: Celiac-specific coping strategies of parents of children with celiac disease
summary: An exploratory study of parents’ responses to the demands of a child’s chronic condition.

name: Charlotte Rösel
title: Mental healthcare for trans and nonbinary clients in Austria
summary: An exploratory qualitative study of perspectives on mental healthcare structures and provision.

name: Anne Walentowski
title: Psychotherapy for refugees: Racism from psychologists’ and psychotherapists’ perspectives
summary: Explores how practitioners understand the role of racism in psychotherapy with refugees.

name: Klara Seltsam
title: Secondary and new antisemitism as defense against guilt and shame
summary: A longitudinal study examining antisemitism in relation to guilt and shame.

name: Jill Ploen
title: Perceived religious discrimination and flourishing: Rumination and co-rumination
summary: Studies individual and interpersonal thinking about distress in relation to discrimination and wellbeing.

name: Dana Goldberg
title: Perceived and experienced antisemitism and wellbeing among Jews in Germany
summary: Examines antisemitic experiences together with social support, identification, and coping.

name: Anna Ross
title: The psychological compensatory benefit of sex work: A mixed-method study in Germany
summary: Combines methods to examine psychological experiences in the context of sex work.

name: Franziska Witte
title: Worries and political engagement from early to middle adulthood
summary: Uses the German Longitudinal Peace Movement Study to examine links between worries and political engagement.

name: Joanna Oath
title: Does xenophobic talk increase negative attitudes toward social outgroups?
summary: Examines the relationship between exclusionary discourse and attitudes toward other social groups.

name: Daniel Lobenhofer
title: Protest tactics and support for protesters: Constructive intentions and disruption
summary: Examines how the perceived intentions and disruptive character of protest shape bystander responses.
award: Best Paper Prize, Association of Psychologists in Osnabrück

name: Shirin Meinhardt
title: Racism and mental health in Germany: Identity, disidentification, and support
summary: Examines religious identity, national disidentification, and social support in relation to discrimination and psychological health.

name: Gitte Arend
title: Workplace racism, discrimination, and psychological health among minorities in Germany
summary: Examines the psychological correlates of discrimination experienced in working life.
